entities.summary:
Bartolomeo Borghesi (1781–1860) was a towering figure in 19th-century Italian antiquarianism, whose meticulous scholarship fundamentally transformed numismatics from a dilettante's pursuit into a rigorous scientific discipline. Born in Savignano sul Rubicone, Italy, he dedicated his life to the systematic study of ancient coins and inscriptions, establishing methodologies that would underpin the nascent fields of epigraphy and classical archaeology across Europe. His work provided critical dating and contextualization for countless artifacts, thereby enriching the understanding of the Roman world for generations of historians and scholars.

Borghesi's most profound contributions stemmed from his unparalleled ability to analyze vast quantities of numismatic and epigraphic data, often correcting long-held errors and establishing new chronological sequences. He meticulously studied the coinage of the Roman Republic and Empire, demonstrating how subtle variations in iconography, legends, and metrology could reveal precise historical information. His groundbreaking work on the `Corpus Inscriptionum Latinarum` began to lay the groundwork for a comprehensive collection of Roman inscriptions, a project later brought to fruition by Theodor Mommsen. Borghesi’s vast personal collection of coins and inscriptions, along with his extensive notes and correspondence, became an indispensable resource for scholars.
